title: The Teardown 003 — One hook, no more commits on main
description: Anthropic published how it builds software with agents. The part worth stealing is one sentence: a skill is advisory, a hook is deterministic. Here is the hook that ended direct commits on main across this operation, with the before-and-after count, plus the artifact chain the playbook is actually about and the one claim in it with the least evidence behind it.
og_title: One hook, no more commits on main — The Teardown 003
og_description: The 69-line Claude Code hook that ended direct commits on main here, the before-and-after from git log, and Anthropic's SDLC playbook torn down: six stages, one commit per handoff, and the one thing the agent is never allowed to do.
og_alt: The artifact chain: Plan commits intent.md, Design commits spec.md, Build commits plan.md and the diff, Test commits evals, Deploy commits a merged PR behind a human approval gate, Maintain commits an incident record that writes the next intent.md
